speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand you're experiencing persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and have a history of easy bruising. To help determine the cause, could you tell me if you have any family members with similar bleeding issues, and have you ever noticed prolonged bleeding from minor cuts or nosebleeds in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. The family history of your uncle suggests a potential hereditary bleeding disorder. Have you ever experienced prolonged bleeding after other surgeries, vaccinations, or dental work, and do you recall any episodes of spontaneous joint swelling or bleeding?

The pattern of bleeding and joint swelling in your family strongly suggests a clotting factor deficiency. I will now order specific coagulation studies to differentiate between Hemophilia A and B.

REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_Activity
REQUEST TEST: Factor_IX_Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: Those normal factor levels are surprising given the history of joint swelling, which typically points to hemophilia. Have you ever noticed bleeding from your gums or nose without any obvious cause, and do you have any personal history of joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, takes no medications. Social history: The patient is a high school student with no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal factor VIII and IX levels rule out classic hemophilia, so we need to look at the clotting cascade's initial phases. I will request tests for the extrinsic and common pathways to narrow this down further.

REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin_Time
REQUEST TEST: Partial_Thromboplastin_Time

speaker: Doctor
text:
The prolonged PTT with a normal PT indicates an issue with the intrinsic pathway, such as a deficiency in factor XI, XII, or von Willebrand disease. Given the history of mucosal bleeding (gums) and easy bruising rather than deep joint bleeds, von Willebrand disease is a strong possibility. I will request specific tests for von Willebrand factor and platelet function to confirm.

REQUEST TEST: von_Willebrand_Factor_Antigen
REQUEST TEST: Ristocetin_Cofactor_Activity

speaker: Doctor
text:
The low von Willebrand factor antigen and ristocetin cofactor activity levels confirm the diagnosis of von Willebrand disease, which aligns with your symptoms of mucosal bleeding and easy bruising.

DIAGNOSIS READY: von Willebrand disease
